items.prompt: GET /api/tickets/:id hides internal notes from a VIEWER. How can a viewer still read them?
items.answer: PATCH tags: the write response returns every comment unfiltered
distractors: By requesting the ticket list, which includes the full comment thread for every row
They cannot; a Prisma middleware applies the visibility filter to every query
By posting an internal note
items.explanation: Only getTicket overrides the comments include with visibleCommentWhere; write responses reuse the raw include (finding 1).

items.prompt: A request reaches /api/tickets with no x-tenant-slug or x-user-email header. Who is it treated as?
distractors: Nobody: it gets 401 because both identity headers are required
A read-only viewer
The first admin user of the first tenant, ordered by creation date
items.explanation: Header-based demo auth with defaults means an anonymous request is an agent: intentionally temporary, but worth knowing.

items.prompt: An agent PATCHes a NEW ticket to CLOSED. Which status code comes back, and why?
items.answer: 500: the domain throws a plain Error
distractors: 409, the conventional conflict response for an invalid status transition
403, because agents may never close tickets from any status
400 from Zod
items.explanation: assertTicketTransition throws a plain Error, and the error middleware maps only ZodError (400) and HttpError (its status) to client codes; everything else becomes 500. Throw an HttpError(409) or map a domain error class instead.

items.prompt: From which statuses may an AGENT move a ticket to CLOSED?
items.answer: Only RESOLVED or PENDING: agents get a special case before the shared transition table is consulted
distractors: OPEN, PENDING or RESOLVED, the same as any other role
None
Any status at all, because agents bypass the transition table
items.explanation: canTransitionTicket special-cases to === CLOSED for agents before consulting the shared table (which also allows OPEN -> CLOSED for others).

items.prompt: A VIEWER sends PATCH with status equal to the ticket's current status. Does assertTicketTransition stop it?
items.answer: No: from === to returns true first
distractors: Yes: viewers can never send a status field in a PATCH request
Yes: same-status moves are always rejected by the domain package
Only if CLOSED
items.explanation: Order of checks matters: the identity shortcut comes first, so a viewer's no-op status passes.

items.prompt: Two tickets are created concurrently in the same tenant. What can happen?
items.answer: Both pick the same next number; the second fails the unique index with a 500
distractors: Nothing: the transaction serializes the two reads
Both succeed with duplicate numbers, because there is no unique index on number
The second silently receives number + 2 through an automatic retry
items.explanation: Reading 'highest + 1' inside a READ COMMITTED transaction does not reserve the number; use a sequence/counter row or retry on conflict.

items.prompt: The database is unreachable for one polling pass, so findMany throws. What happens to the worker?
items.answer: Polling ends for good, because the loop's promise rejects before setTimeout schedules the next pass
distractors: It retries the same pass after the configured poll interval
It marks every pending event FAILED and then continues polling
Node restarts the worker process automatically after the crash
items.explanation: The loop's promise rejects before setTimeout schedules the next pass; only per-event errors are caught. Wrapping processOutboxBatch in try/catch and always rescheduling keeps the worker alive.

items.prompt: You start two worker processes. What happens to each PENDING event?
items.answer: Both may process it: there is no claim step
distractors: Exactly one worker, thanks to the PROCESSING status
The second worker blocks on a row lock until the first one finishes the event
Prisma's findMany skips rows that another connection has already read
items.explanation: Selecting PENDING then updating by id is not a claim; FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED with RETURNING is the suggested fix.

items.prompt: An event's handler throws once and is marked FAILED. When is it retried?
items.answer: Never: only PENDING events are selected
distractors: On the next poll, up to five attempts in total
After an exponential backoff computed from the attempts counter
When the API writes the next outbox event for the same ticket
items.explanation: FAILED is terminal; a crash between the two status updates also leaves events stuck in PROCESSING.

items.prompt: What classic bug does writing an OutboxEvent in the same transaction as the ticket change prevent?
items.answer: A saved change whose notification is lost unrecorded
distractors: Two agents editing the same ticket at the same moment
Customers receiving notifications rendered in the wrong time zone
The worker reading uncommitted ticket data from another transaction
items.explanation: Writing the OutboxEvent in the same transaction means the change and its pending side effect commit or roll back together; the classic bug is a DB write that succeeds while the notification fails before anything records that it still needs sending.

items.prompt: A NORMAL ticket created 20 hours ago is raised to URGENT. When is it now due?
items.answer: Two hours from now, because slaDueAt is recalculated from the current time
distractors: Already breached: two hours after creation was 18 hours ago
Still 4 hours from now: the original NORMAL deadline is kept
Two hours from the last customer reply on the ticket
items.explanation: When the priority changes, updateTicket recalculates slaDueAt with calculateSlaDueAt(new Date(), priority), i.e. from now, not from creation.

items.prompt: Two agents post the first public reply at the same moment. Why can firstResponseAt be overwritten?
items.answer: It is read before the transaction, so both see null and both write
distractors: The WHERE firstResponseAt IS NULL guard is ignored by Prisma
Because internal notes also set firstResponseAt when they are the first comment
It cannot; the comment insert locks the ticket row until the transaction commits
items.explanation: The check is outside the transaction and the update is unconditional by id; a conditional update (where firstResponseAt: null) would make the first writer win.

items.front: Which write actions are open to a VIEWER in the support desk?
items.back: Creating tickets, changing priority or tags, posting public replies to customers and ingesting email. Only status changes and assignment are checked; requireRole guards just the audit-log route.

PENDING, RESOLVED and CLOSED are PAUSED; no due date is MET; past due is BREACHED; within one hour of due is AT_RISK; otherwise MET. Leaving PENDING keeps the original slaDueAt, so paused time still counts.

items.front: Two upgrades that make the outbox worker production-shaped
items.back: Retry: add availableAt and select status in (PENDING, FAILED) with attempts < 5 and availableAt <= now. Claim: UPDATE ... SET status = 'PROCESSING' WHERE id IN (SELECT ... FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED LIMIT 10) RETURNING * so concurrent workers never share an event.

items.front: What happens to the domain package's visibility rule in practice?
items.back: canViewInternalNote and canManageUsers exist but are unused; the visibility rule is re-implemented inline in visibleCommentWhere, so the domain package and the service can drift apart.
